question: Which of the following is called the amphibian of the plant kingdom?
solution:
The answer is __**Bryophyta**__.

__
 
• **In the plant kingdom, bryophytes are known as amphibians.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efb90c3647c276e117dc17fb6439410dad00fafe8f511a89c38f32cba7de65df.png] 

 
• **Bryophytes:**

 
 
• **A bryophyte is a nonvascular plant that is green, seedless and belongs to the mosses, liverworts, or hornworts family.**
 
• Bryophytes are among the **simplest of terrestrial plants.**
 
• **In Bryophyta, there is a lack of xylem and phloem tissue.**
 
• **They lack true roots, stem and leaves.**
 
• **Bryophytes are known as the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they live in the soil but need water to reproduce sexually.**
 
• They prefer moist, humid, and shady environments.
 
• **On bare rocks/soil, they serve a vital role in plant succession.**
 
• **Figure: Moss**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e190e36ebfffcb5d962ac8f40c45f2e97a7a4a2ed14d5b3d9f601dc2838ad19.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thallophyta:****​**

 
 
• **A division of the plant kingdom that contained plants that were relatively simple, i.e. those that had no leaves, stems, or roots.**
 
• **It included algae, bacteria, fungi, and lichens.**
 
• **Algae:**
 
 
• The term algae refer to many types of aquatic, photosynthetic organisms.
 
• **Algae are simple and green,** growing as scum in watery places like ponds, lakes, drains, wet soil, seashores.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Cryptogam:**
 
 
• **Cryptogams are plants or plant-like organisms that reproduce by spores** rather than flowers or seeds.
 
• Cryptogams are plants that do not produce seed.
 
• **Examples:** 
 
 
• Algae, lichens, mosses and ferns
 
 
 
 
 
• **Phanerogam:**
 
 
• **The spermatophytes also known as phanerogams, comprise those plants that produce seeds.**
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• ​Coconut, maize, banana, mustard, pea, mango, grass
